name: Incorrect Privilege Assignment
title: CWE-266: Incorrect Privilege Assignment
ai_text: In AI software, CWE-266 shows up in agent frameworks, MCP servers and low code LLM builders, where roles and approvals are handed out too loosely. The CVEs sit in Flowise, Langflow and NanoClaw. The usual way in is an ordinary signed-in account or a local user, not a remote stranger. Flowise before 3.1.4 lets any signed-in user become owner of another organization. Langflow 1.0.0 to 1.10.3 lets a logged-in user reach host files through Docker MCP servers. NanoClaw up to 2.0.64 has an MCP approval flaw that lets a local user bypass authorization. The result is an unintended sphere of control, so a low privileged user gains owner rights, host file access or approval bypass.
description: A product incorrectly assigns a privilege to a particular actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

mitigations.description: Very carefully manage the setting, management, and handling of privileges. Explicitly manage trust zones in the software.

Run your code using the lowest privileges that are required to accomplish the necessary tasks [REF-76]. If possible, create isolated accounts with limited privileges that are only used for a single task. That way, a successful attack will not immediately give the attacker access to the rest of the software or its environment. For example, database applications rarely need to run as the database administrator, especially in day-to-day operations.

consequences.note: A user can access restricted functionality and/or sensitive information that may include administrative functionality and user accounts.
